title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRDs, Roadmap & Pricing (Q4 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document is the consolidated product reference for Redwood Inference's Unified Inference initiative (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private). It covers the product overview, high-level PRDs and requirements for priority features, design specs, roadmap and themes through Q2 2027, pricing and packaging recommendations, and release notes for the v2026.09 product milestone. Intended audience: product managers, engineering leads, solutions, sales engineering, and docs.

1) Overview

Redwood Unified Inference is Redwood's product vision to provide a single, consistent developer experience for model serving across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The focus for the next two quarters is: predictable latency and cost controls, rollout tooling, and deeper integrations for enterprise security and observability. Key customer scenarios: conversational applications with strict latency, search/reranking at scale, and regulated on-prem inference.

Goals & success metrics (90 days / 180 days):
- Reduce median token latency for typical chat workloads by 15% on hosted API (baseline: 95ms for 512-token warm requests).
- Reduce per-token cost for business-critical batch workloads by 20% through batching + caching recommendations.
- Increase private deployment adoption: close 3 pilot deals (>=$200k ACV) by Q2 2027.
- Launch pricing & packaging aligned to usage and reserved capacity (see Pricing section).

2) Scope (in/out)

In scope:
- Model routing / cost-aware fallbacks (hosted + dedicated).
- Redwood Optimize v6 recommendations surfaced in Console and API.
- Billing primitives for reserved capacity and per-route pricing.
- Console UI for rollout policies and canarying.

Out of scope (this release):
- New model training or model building features.
- Third-party marketplace integrations.

3) High-level PRD (features & requirements)

Requirement matrix:
| Requirement | Priority | Owner | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Cost-aware model routing (API-level policy) | P0 | Product: Model Routing | Routing policy can be applied per-route; fallbacks execute within 50ms; end-to-end cost reduction observable in staging workload. |
| Reserved capacity billing primitives | P0 | Finance & Product | Billing shows committed vs used capacity; invoices include committed discount; test invoice generated in staging. |
| Autoscaling for Dedicated with burst buckets | P1 | Eng-Infrastructure | Dedicated pools support a configurable burst pool with defined thresholds and cooldowns; documented in runbook. |
| Console rollout controls (canary & A/B) | P0 | Product: Console | Users can define canary % by route, compare metrics for canary vs control, rollback in <3 clicks. |
| Quality monitoring tied to evals | P1 | Applied ML | Per-deployment eval sets can be attached; quality regression alert fires on 5% drop in evaluation score. |

User stories (selected):
1. As a product engineer, I can pin a route to a cheaper quantized model and fall back to a higher-quality model if latency exceeds SLOs.
2. As an infra owner, I can allocate reserved capacity to a team and see projected monthly spend and utilization.
3. As an SRE, I can run a canary deploy on 5% of traffic and compare latency and token-cost metrics in the Console.

Non-functional requirements:
- API backward compatibility: existing generation and embedding endpoints must retain contract for 99.95% of calls.
- Security: Private deployments must support customer KMS and audit-log integration.
- Reliability: SLOs targeted in Operational Readiness section below.

4) Design specs (implementation notes)

Design constraints and decisions:
- Single routing decision: make routing decision centrally in the Edge Router service to avoid duplicated state. Decision record to follow in architecture-and-standards.
- Cache semantics: prefix/KV caching implemented in the serving runtime; Console exposes TTL and cache-hit metrics.

High-level architecture (textual):
- Edge Router: receives API requests, applies per-route policy (latency, cost, region), selects serving backends.
- Serving Runtime: optimized, GPU-aware engine with quantization support and KV cache.
- Orchestration Layer: manages Dedicated pools, autoscaling, and private deployments.
- Billing & Usage Pipeline: consumes request telemetry, applies pricing rules, and populates billing UI.

Example policy (YAML):
```yaml
route: "/chat/completion"
policies:
  - name: cost-aware-routing
    priority: 10
    rules:
      - metric: latency_p50_ms
        operator: "<="
        value: 120
        action:
          backend: fast-quantized-v1
      - metric: latency_p95_ms
        operator: ">"
        value: 200
        action:
          backend: high-quality-v3
```

Design checklist for engineers:
- [ ] Edge Router accepts per-route JSON/YAML policy and validates schema.
- [ ] Serving runtime exposes cache control hooks and cache telemetry.
- [ ] Billing pipeline adds committed_capacity fields for Dedicated customers.
- [ ] Console surfaces rollouts and canary metrics with guided rollback.

5) Roadmap & Themes (Q4 2026 -> Q2 2027)

Themes by quarter:
- Q4 2026: Cost Controls & Routing (cost-aware fallbacks, reserved capacity billing, initial Console rollout controls).
- Q1 2027: Dedicated Autoscaling & Observability (burst buckets, deeper trace linking, per-token cost at route level).
- Q2 2027: Private deployment maturity (KMS, audit integrations, on-prem packaging improvements) and enterprise sales enablement.

Milestones (high level):
- 2026-09-20: v2026.09 release (see Release Notes section).
- 2026-11-15: Console rollout controls GA for hosted customers.
- 2027-02-15: Dedicated burst autoscaling beta.
- 2027-05-01: Private deployment KMS + audit logging GA.

6) Pricing & Packaging notes

Pricing goals:
- Align incentives: customers who commit to capacity get predictable unit pricing.
- Support mixed-mode customers (hosted + dedicated + private) with clear blended billing.

Proposed pricing primitives:
- On-demand (hosted API): per-request per-token priced tiers: Standard, Pro, Enterprise.
- Reserved Capacity (Dedicated): monthly commit with tiered discount (10% at 3-month, 20% at 12-month commit).
- Route-level pricing: ability to mark routes as high-priority (higher unit price but guaranteed latency).

Example pricing table (simplified):
| Tier | Unit price (per 1k tokens) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Standard (hosted) | $0.30 | Default public API tier. |
| Pro (hosted) | $0.20 | For accounts > $5k monthly. Includes 30-day retention for request-level logs. |
| Dedicated (reserved) | $0.12 | Committed capacity; sliding discount for term length. |

Billing examples (illustrative):
- Customer A: 100M tokens/month on Pro => $20k/month.
- Customer B: Reserved 500 GPU-hours/month with 12-month commit => applied reserved discount; invoice shows committed vs overage.

Packaging guidance for Sales:
- SMB / PLG: promote Standard + Optimize recommendations; low friction signup.
- Mid-market: Pro + 3-month reserved capacity trial.
- Enterprise: Dedicated or Private + Premium Support, contract terms for retention and SLAs.

7) Release notes: v2026.09 (public)

Highlights:
- GA: Cost-aware model routing (beta enabled for selected customers during preview).
- Feature: Console — rollout controls (canary and simple A/B).
- Billing: Reserved capacity primitives (invoice preview in Console staging).
- Perf: end-to-end median token latency improvement of 12% on small conversational models.

Known issues and workarounds:
- Some customers with extreme long-sequence workloads may observe reduced cache hit rates after routing changes. Workaround: increase cache TTL for route and pin to compatible model.
- Billing preview for multi-tenant reserved capacity shows duplication in staging; fix targeted for 2026-10-10.

Deprecations: none for this release.

8) Rollout plan & risk mitigation

Phased rollout (hosted):
1. Internal dogfood (2 weeks) — enable features for internal teams, collect telemetry.
2. Beta customers (4-6 weeks) — opt-in list, monitor cost, latency, and quality.
3. Gradual ramp to GA (2-4 weeks) — 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic increments with automatic rollback triggers.

Automatic rollback triggers (example):
- P50 latency regression > 40% over baseline for 5 minutes.
- Error rate increase > 1% absolute for 10 minutes.
- Model quality drop > 5% on attached eval set.

Communication plan:
- Release notes email to customers and partner Slack channels.
- Sales enablement deck + pricing cheat sheet.
- Migration guide and FAQ in product-docs.

9) Operational readiness & SLOs

SLOs (initial):
- API availability: 99.95% per month.
- Median token latency (hosted chat, 512 tokens): <= 120ms (p50).
- Billing accuracy: invoice generation within 24 hours for committed reporting.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Dashboards: per-route latency, cost-per-token, cache-hit, fallback-rate.
- Alerts: increased fallback rate > 10% triggers oncall.

Runbooks and playbooks to update: eng-sre/runbooks, eng-serving-runtime/runbooks, eng-platform/runbooks.

10) Ownership and next steps

Primary owners:
- Product: Aisha Patel (overall), Product leads: Luca Moretti (Routing), Hannah Cho (Console).
- Eng leads: Matteo Ricci (Edge Router), Priya Singh (Serving Runtime), Aaron Kim (Billing).
- Applied ML: Dr. Elena Garcia (Quality & evals).

Next actions (30 days):
- Finalize API schema for per-route policy (Responsible: Matteo Ricci, due: 2026-09-30).
- Implement billing committed_capacity field and staging invoice generator (Responsible: Aaron Kim, due: 2026-10-10).
- Prepare sales enablement materials and pricing table (Responsible: Marketing & Sales Engineering, due: 2026-10-05).

Appendix

```bash
redwood rollout create --route "/chat/completion" --policy canary --percent 5 --compare-metrics latency,error_rate
```
